independence: Reviewer authored the late-half proposal, not the 279 early-half records under review. Actual early learner text and paradigms were read independently; proposal quotations and hashes did not substitute for source reading.
scope: Pronunciation and Units 1–9 entries as represented in the merged grammatical-topic index; term/topic accuracy, teaching/reference/supplied scope, exact source-target relevance, aliases and see-also links. No learner or source-master edits.

grammar_register.use: Cross-checked relevant reference/missing-form/supplied feature descriptions with the actual text; printed locations are determined from learner prose and paradigms.

source_reading.review_note: Read the actual vowel/consonant tables and articulation prose. Length, stress, weight, diphthong syllabification, conditional voicing and audible unstressed vowels are correctly distinguished.

Read full nominal/copular exposition and paradigms. Supplied finite verbs support productive case choices; reconstructed sea genitive plural and instrumental cells remain reference. Neuter weight and lexical stem exceptions are not universalized.

Read complete pronouns and weak indicative systems and ordinary uses. Dual agreement, personal genitives, lexical government and recognition-only nabban are accurate. Three detailed entries need the nearby contrast-list locator (BIE-01).

Read adjective, possessive, comparative, numeral and demonstrative rules and complete relevant tables. Strong/weak and reference limits are retained. V/C-stem label is misleading (BIE-02); instrumental entry omits demonstrative targets (BIE-03).

Read all principal-part, present/preterite and noun explanations and paradigms. Contracted and exceptional verbs, second-singular preterites, recognition-only systems and object government have accurate entries.
Read all Class IV–VII exposition/paradigms and ordinary uses. Nasal exceptions, palatal quantities, j-present consonants, contracted verbs and citation-only participles are correctly bounded.

Read complete irregular indicatives and all infinitive/command model tables and uses. Missing modal nonfinite forms, ordinary capability/permission versus mood, expected/habitual be, selected infinitive endings and shortened plural command reference are accurately indexed.

Read complete subjunctive and additional verb systems, conditional examples, all five complete participle models, passive variation and quantifier/function teaching. The nonpast preterite condition remains supplied recognition; model completeness does not imply unrestricted syntax.

Read all interrogative/pronominal paradigms, relative explanations and indexed lexical frames. Ge-compound/instrumental reference, case attraction and personal-pronoun relative strategies remain reference; inflected relatives preserve antecedent agreement and internal case.

Read all indexed finite/infinitive complement, wish, preference and partitive explanations, the three new noun-class paradigms, adjective agreement tables and final construction notes. Mood tendencies, present unreal wishes, actor/object distinctions and reference-only singular manig are retained.

findings.problem: The label vowel- and consonant-ending stems misdefines V-stem/C-stem as a classification of stem-final sounds. The teaching defines the stem selected before a vowel-initial or consonant-initial ending.
findings.supporting_quote: V-stem is used before endings beginning with a vowel: -es, -um, -e, -a and -an. C-stem is used before -ne, -re and -ra.
findings.repair: Use stem variants before vowel and consonant endings; the application-map target itself is suitable.
findings.coordinator_response: Accepted; terminology correction will be recorded as an index amendment against the contract hash.

resolution.verified: The final label is stem variants before vowel and consonant endings, accurately describing selection by the following ending. The application-map target remains unchanged.
